Global Corporate Data Retention and Privacy Governance Framework (SEC-POL-2026)
Corporate Policy SEC-POL-2026: Information Security & Data Governance
Effective Date: January 1, 2026 | Authority: Global Data Protection Office
Scope: All enterprise cloud infrastructure, relational databases, vector storage, and distributed services.
Clause SEC-4.1.2: Mandatory Encryption of Data at Rest
All enterprise production data stored in persistent relational databases, vector indexes, and object stores
must be encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM encryption. Cryptographic envelope keys must be rotated
every 90 days under automated hardware security module (HSM) control. Unencrypted storage of
sensitive data is strictly prohibited.
Clause SEC-4.2.1: Data Classification Tiering
Enterprise data is partitioned into two regulatory tiers:
? TIER-1 RESTRICTED: Personally Identifiable Information (PII), customer payment instruments, medical
records, and master credentials.
? TIER-2 CONFIDENTIAL: Internal architectural specifications, non-public source code, financial
forecasts, and internal communications.

Clause AUD-9.0.1: Mandatory Annual Compliance Audits
The enterprise must undergo formal independent third-party SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliance
examinations every 12 months. Audit reports must be reviewed by the Board Audit Committee and
maintained on file for 5 years.
Clause AUD-9.2.3: Non-Compliance Penalties and Enforcement
Violations of this framework are categorized into three severity levels. A Level-3 critical compliance breach
triggers immediate executive committee intervention and mandates formal notification to regulatory
supervisory authorities within 72 hours of incident confirmation. Willful non-compliance may result in
disciplinary termination and civil liability.
Clause AUD-9.4.0: Policy Review and Revision Cadence
This policy document is subject to mandatory annual re-certification every November by the Chief
Information Security Officer.

AetherDB Distributed Cluster Administration Guide v3.4 · Architecture (Page 1)
Section 1.1: Distributed Consensus & Network Topology
AetherDB v3.4 is an enterprise-grade distributed key-value and vector database engine. The cluster
operates on a Raft consensus gossip protocol across 3 to 7 nodes per regional zone. Client RPC
applications connect exclusively to Port 9092 for read and write operations. Inter-node consensus, leader
election, and log replication communicate over Port 9093. Cluster telemetry, health probes, and
Prometheus metrics are exposed via HTTP on Port 8080.
Section 1.2: Quorum Mechanics & Fault Tolerance
Cluster write consensus requires a strict majority quorum formulated as (N / 2) + 1 active nodes, where N
represents the total configured cluster voting membership. For a 5-node cluster, a quorum of 3 nodes is
mandatory to commit any write transaction to the write-ahead log (WAL). If two nodes fail, the cluster
continues operating seamlessly. If three nodes fail, the cluster enters read-only protective mode.

Section 3.1: Critical Error Codes and Recovery Playbooks
The cluster telemetry subsystem emits standardized alphanumeric error codes when operational
anomalies arise:
Error Code ERR_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_0x7A:
Indicates that the inbound socket buffer exceeded the 64MB queue capacity during an unexpected traffic
surge. Diagnostic procedure: Verify connection pooling metrics and increase --rx-buffer-mb=128 or scale
out client worker nodes.
Error Code ERR_RAFT_SPLIT_BRAIN_0x9F:
Signals that multiple leaders were concurrently detected due to an asymmetrical network partition across
WAN links. Diagnostic procedure: Check firewall rules on Port 9093, isolate the minority partition, and
restart isolated nodes.
Error Code ERR_TLS_CERT_EXPIRED_0x3C:

procedure: Renew the internal root CA certificate bundle and execute the aetherdb-cert-reload CLI utility.

Section 3.1: Critical Error Codes and Recovery Playbooks
The cluster telemetry subsystem emits standardized alphanumeric error codes when operational
anomalies arise:
Error Code ERR_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_0x7A:
Indicates that the inbound socket buffer exceeded the 64MB queue capacity during an unexpected traffic
surge. Diagnostic procedure: Verify connection pooling metrics and increase --rx-buffer-mb=128 or scale
out client worker nodes.
Error Code ERR_RAFT_SPLIT_BRAIN_0x9F:
Signals that multiple leaders were concurrently detected due to an asymmetrical network partition across
WAN links. Diagnostic procedure: Check firewall rules on Port 9093, isolate the minority partition, and
restart isolated nodes.
Error Code ERR_TLS_CERT_EXPIRED_0x3C:
Occurs when inter-node mutual TLS certificate validation fails due to certificate expiration. Diagnostic
procedure: Renew the internal root CA certificate bundle and execute the aetherdb-cert-reload CLI utility.

Section 4.1: Automated Failover Protocols
Automatic leader failover initiates within 750ms when a Raft leader misses 3 consecutive heartbeat
intervals (3 * 250ms). The candidate node with the most up-to-date log index receives affirmative votes
from remaining quorum members and assumes the leader role without dropping in-flight client read
requests.
Section 4.2: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
When configured in synchronous replication mode (sync_replication=true), AetherDB guarantees a
Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of zero, meaning zero data loss upon single-node or zone failure.
